q1.answer: Backstage decided that any fetch/XMLHttpRequest in tests should be mocked with msw, which declares express-style route handlers at the network level instead of stubbing fetch directly (the approach react-testing-library recommends). Tests then exercise the real request path, and mocking stays consistent across test types.

q2.answer: ADR014 (Proper use of HTTP fetching libraries, which supersedes ADR013's node-fetch guidance) says frontend plugins should prefer fetchApiRef and that clients should accept an injected fetch, so callers can supply their own implementation that adds auth or other information and tracks metrics. Third-party fetch packages are being phased out.

q3.answer: ADR010 makes Luxon the standard Backstage date library for date formatting and calculations (such as 'a day ago') that native Date doesn't handle well. Moment.js has large bundles and mutable state and is being sunset, while Luxon is immutable, built on Intl and lighter, and one shared library means one API to learn and smaller bundles.

q4.answer: ADR006 says to avoid React.FC/SFC in new code, following create-react-app's removal of it, because it adds little and has downsides: it implicitly adds children props and doesn't support generics on children. Components should instead type their props parameter explicitly.

q5.answer: ADR004 requires every exported symbol to be traceable through index files up to src/index.ts, with each index file re-exporting only its immediate children and only index files doing re-exports. That way you can tell whether a symbol is public by following the index chain, and the package boundary stays predictable instead of a mix of deep re-exports.
